correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the shared Poisson gaps yields a product of independent Brownian survival factors. The zero/one reset expansion gives the exact coefficient, while the two-or-more-reset probability is O((rt)^2). Under d2^2>=6Dt the target first-hit CDF is convex and the far target's one-reset response strictly positive. The near-target convolution estimate d1^2/D and explicit erfc lower bound force the coefficient strictly negative for a nonempty distance interval. Same distances give strictly positive clock-variance for every r>0. Checker evaluates only numerical examples; all universals proved analytically.

originality.rationale: Inspected the 2026 main paper sections II.1–II.2, IV.1, IV.4, 2023 global-reset first-arrival article (including protocol B and appendix), and 2023 resetting-gas abstract. None of these inspected materials states or implies the negative heterogeneous fixed-horizon cross-survival indicator coefficient in the submitted theorem. Compared to earlier same-distance hitting-time covariance work, the observable and heterogeneity differ essentially. General common-clock mixture conditioning is known, and is not claimed novel. Novelty is qualified by residual general-dependence-theorem risk.
residual_risks: A general theorem on conditional common-environment survival association may already imply the sign reversal in a different form.
Full text of 2023 spatial gas and 2025 event-triggered resetting gas was not inspected; different observables/model make direct coverage less likely.

value.rationale: Heterogeneous geometry in rank-resolved resetting experiments makes the sign of induced dependence meaningful, not merely the existence of correlation. The proven negative regime defeats homogeneous positive-association assumptions despite strictly independent Brownian motions and only a shared external clock. This supplies a structural counterboundary for variance and joint-arrival modeling, not a routine reformulation of known mean first-passage optimization.
